osces.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome - STEMI Management
osces.scenario: You are the emergency physician on call. A 58-year-old male plumber presents to ED with sudden-onset severe central chest pain that started 45 minutes ago while lifting heavy pipes at work. The pain is crushing in nature, radiates to his left arm and jaw, and is associated with diaphoresis and nausea. He has a history of hypertension and is a current smoker (30 pack-years). His wife drove him to hospital immediately. Vital signs: BP 145/90, HR 95, RR 20, SpO2 96% on room air, temp 36.8°C. He appears pale and diaphoretic.

patient_presentation.chief_complaint: Severe crushing central chest pain for 45 minutes
patient_presentation.history: 58-year-old male plumber with sudden-onset severe central chest pain while lifting heavy equipment. Pain is 9/10, crushing, radiates to left arm and jaw. Associated with diaphoresis, nausea, and feeling of impending doom. No previous episodes. Current smoker 30 pack-years. Takes amlodipine 10mg daily for hypertension. No known allergies.
patient_presentation.examination_findings: Appears distressed, pale, diaphoretic. Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no murmurs. JVP not elevated. No peripheral oedema. Chest: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Peripheral pulses present and equal.

ecg.findings: Sinus rhythm at 95 bpm. ST elevation 4mm in leads II, III, aVF. Reciprocal ST depression 2mm in leads I, aVL. Q waves not yet present. QT interval 420ms (normal).
ecg.interpretation: Acute inferior STEMI - likely RCA occlusion

investigations.chest_xray: Normal heart size, clear lung fields, no acute pathology

management_tasks.details: Give aspirin 300mg PO stat, ticagrelor 180mg PO stat loading dose, atorvastatin 80mg PO stat. Commence IV access and continuous cardiac monitoring.
Door-to-balloon time target <90 minutes. Contact interventional cardiology team immediately. If PCI not available within 90 minutes, consider thrombolysis with tenecteplase.
Commence enoxaparin 1mg/kg SC BD or bivalirudin if going for primary PCI. Avoid unfractionated heparin due to bleeding risk.
Morphine 2.5mg IV PRN for pain relief. Metoprolol 25mg BD PO once haemodynamically stable. Monitor for complications (arrhythmias, heart failure, mechanical complications).

osces.title: Inferior STEMI with Right Heart Involvement - Primary PCI Decision Making
osces.scenario: You are the emergency physician on duty when a 58-year-old truck driver presents to your regional hospital emergency department with severe chest pain. The nearest PCI-capable centre is 45 minutes away by road ambulance. You need to assess, diagnose, and initiate appropriate management including making critical decisions about reperfusion strategy.

patient_presentation.chief_complaint: Severe central chest pain for 90 minutes, described as crushing and radiating to jaw
patient_presentation.history_present_illness: 58-year-old male truck driver developed sudden onset severe central chest pain at 0800 hours while loading his truck. Pain is crushing in nature, 9/10 severity, radiating to jaw and left arm. Associated with nausea, vomiting, and diaphoresis. No relief with rest. Pain has been constant for 90 minutes. No previous episodes of similar pain. Denied shortness of breath initially but now reports mild dyspnoea.
patient_presentation.past_medical_history: Hypertension (diagnosed 5 years ago), hypercholesterolaemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus (well controlled), ex-smoker (quit 2 years ago, 30 pack-year history). Father died of MI at age 62.
patient_presentation.medications: Perindopril 5mg daily, atorvastatin 40mg nocte, metformin 1000mg BD, aspirin 100mg daily (ceased 3 days ago for dental procedure)
patient_presentation.social_history: Truck driver, sedentary lifestyle, moderate alcohol consumption (2-3 standard drinks daily), lives with wife, no recreational drug use

examination_findings.vital_signs: BP 160/95 mmHg (right arm), 150/90 mmHg (left arm), HR 58 bpm regular, RR 20/min, SpO2 96% on room air, Temperature 36.8°C
examination_findings.cardiovascular: Pulse regular, bradycardic at 58 bpm. JVP elevated at 6cm above sternal angle. Heart sounds: S1 and S2 present, no murmurs audible. Apex beat not displaced. Peripheral pulses present and equal bilaterally. No pedal oedema.
examination_findings.respiratory: Respiratory rate 20/min, mild use of accessory muscles. Chest expansion equal bilaterally. Percussion resonant throughout. Auscultation reveals fine bibasal crackles, otherwise clear.
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen soft, non-tender. Neurological examination grossly normal. Skin cool and clammy. No obvious signs of trauma.

investigations.ecg: 12-lead ECG shows: Rate 58 bpm, regular rhythm. PR interval 180ms. QRS width 90ms. Axis +90 degrees. ST elevation 4mm in leads II (4mm), III (5mm), aVF (4mm). Reciprocal ST depression 2mm in leads I and aVL. ST elevation 2mm in V1, 1mm in V2 (suggestive of posterior involvement). No pathological Q waves yet present.
investigations.chest_xray: Heart size upper limit of normal (cardiothoracic ratio 0.48). Mild pulmonary vascular congestion. No pleural effusions. Lung fields otherwise clear.
investigations.blood_tests: Initial: Hb 142 g/L (120-170), WCC 8.2 x10⁹/L (4.0-11.0), Platelets 285 x10⁹/L (150-450). Na+ 140 mmol/L (135-145), K+ 4.2 mmol/L (3.5-5.0), Creatinine 89 μmol/L (60-110), eGFR >90. Initial troponin I 0.8 μg/L (<0.04), CK 180 U/L (30-200). Glucose 8.2 mmol/L (4.0-7.8).
investigations.echocardiogram: Not immediately available - would show inferior wall hypokinesis with possible RV involvement if performed

osces.diagnosis: Primary diagnosis: Acute inferior STEMI with possible right heart and posterior wall involvement. Differential diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome, acute pericarditis (less likely given ECG changes), aortic dissection (less likely given ECG and examination findings)
immediate_management: Step 1: Immediate - Oxygen if SpO2 <90%, IV access x2, cardiac monitoring, 12-lead ECG repeated every 30 minutes
Step 2: Within 5 minutes - Aspirin 300mg PO stat, ticagrelor 180mg PO stat, atorvastatin 80mg PO stat
Step 3: Within 10 minutes - Contact interventional cardiology team, arrange urgent transfer for primary PCI
Step 4: Pain relief - Morphine 2.5-5mg IV every 5 minutes PRN (monitor respiratory rate)
Step 5: Anticoagulation - Enoxaparin 1mg/kg SC (contraindicated if going to surgery within 8 hours) OR heparin per local protocol
Step 6: Right heart assessment - Right-sided ECG leads (V3R, V4R) to assess RV involvement
Step 7: Transfer preparation - Brief family, obtain consent, ensure continuous monitoring during transfer
australian_guidelines: National Heart Foundation of Australia and Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand: Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes 2016
CSANZ Guidelines: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) 2018 - Door-to-balloon time <90 minutes target
Australian Resuscitation Council Guideline 11.5: Acute Coronary Syndromes
eTG: Cardiovascular - Management of ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care: Acute Coronary Syndrome Clinical Care Standard
learning_objectives: Rapidly recognise and diagnose STEMI from clinical presentation and 12-lead ECG interpretation
Understand the importance of door-to-balloon time <90 minutes and make appropriate reperfusion decisions
Demonstrate knowledge of evidence-based acute STEMI medication management with correct doses
Recognise right heart involvement in inferior STEMI and its management implications
Apply Australian guidelines for primary PCI vs thrombolysis decision-making in regional settings
Understand the role of dual antiplatelet therapy and appropriate anticoagulation in STEMI
osces.examiner_notes: Assessment criteria: 1) Rapid ECG interpretation and STEMI recognition (25%) - must identify inferior STEMI with ST elevations >1mm in leads II, III, aVF and recognise reciprocal changes. 2) Appropriate immediate management sequence (25%) - aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, statin, anticoagulation with correct timing. 3) Primary PCI decision and transfer arrangements (20%) - understand door-to-balloon targets and contact protocols. 4) Medication knowledge (20%) - correct doses and PBS codes for dual antiplatelet therapy. 5) Right heart involvement recognition (10%) - suggest right-sided ECG leads and understand prognostic implications. Pass mark: 70%. Common mistakes: Delaying aspirin, incorrect ticagrelor dosing, missing right heart involvement, choosing thrombolysis when PCI available within time targets.

osces.chief_complaint: Severe central chest pain for 2 hours
osces.history_of_presenting_illness: 58-year-old male tradesperson presents with sudden onset severe central chest pain that began 2 hours ago while at work. examination_findings.respiratory: Fine bibasal crepitations, otherwise clear lung fields. No wheeze.
examination_findings.other_systems: Diaphoretic, appears distressed. Abdomen soft, non-tender. No focal neurological deficits.

investigations.ecg_findings: ST elevation 4mm in leads II, III, aVF with reciprocal ST depression 2mm in leads I, aVL. Q waves developing in lead III. Heart rate 95 bpm, PR interval 160ms, QRS 90ms.
investigations.chest_xray: Mild cardiomegaly, upper lobe blood diversion consistent with mild pulmonary oedema. No consolidation or pneumothorax.

blood_tests.fbc: Hb 142 g/L, WCC 11.2 x10⁹/L, Platelets 280 x10⁹/L
blood_tests.ue: Na 138 mmol/L, K 4.1 mmol/L, Cr 95 μmol/L, eGFR >60
blood_tests.lipids: Total cholesterol 6.2 mmol/L, LDL 4.1 mmol/L, HDL 0.9 mmol/L, TG 3.8 mmol/L

osces.diagnosis: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) - inferior wall with Killip Class II heart failure
immediate_management: Aspirin 300mg PO stat - PBS 8053K
Ticagrelor 180mg PO stat, then 90mg BD - PBS 8721K
Heparin 5000 units IV bolus, then 1000 units/hour - PBS 1679F
Metoprolol 25mg BD PO (once stabilised) - PBS 2937F
High-flow oxygen if SpO2 <90%
IV access x2, continuous cardiac monitoring
Code Blue STEMI activation - target door-to-balloon <90 minutes
Primary PCI with drug-eluting stent to RCA
Morphine 2.5-5mg IV PRN for pain - PBS 1213D
ongoing_management: Dual antiplatelet therapy for 12 months minimum
ACE inhibitor - increase perindopril to 8mg daily
Beta-blocker - titrate metoprolol to maximum tolerated dose
High-intensity statin - increase atorvastatin to 80mg nocte
Diabetes management - consider insulin given HbA1c 8.1%
patient_education: Explanation of heart attack and treatment received
Importance of medication compliance, especially dual antiplatelet therapy
When to seek emergency care (chest pain, shortness of breath)
Lifestyle modifications: smoking cessation maintenance, diet, exercise
Return to work guidelines (light duties for 4-6 weeks)
osces.follow_up: Cardiologist appointment within 1 week post-discharge, GP follow-up within 72 hours, cardiac rehabilitation assessment within 6 weeks, diabetes educator review within 2 weeks
learning_objectives: Recognise clinical presentation of acute STEMI

Implement evidence-based acute management of STEMI
Calculate and apply GRACE risk score for prognosis
Understand primary PCI vs thrombolysis decision-making

Recognise and manage complications of MI

assessment_criteria.criteria: Systematic approach, correct identification of ST elevation in inferior leads, recognition of reciprocal changes, accurate measurements
Correlation of ECG findings with clinical presentation, understanding of coronary anatomy, risk stratification
Appropriate activation of STEMI pathway, correct medication choices with doses, contraindication awareness
Clear explanation of findings, appropriate urgency, patient counselling skills

key_teaching_points: Inferior STEMI typically involves RCA occlusion - leads II, III, aVF show ST elevation with reciprocal changes in I, aVL
Primary PCI is preferred reperfusion strategy if available within 90 minutes of first medical contact
Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor) is cornerstone of medical management in ACS
Door-to-balloon time <90 minutes is quality indicator for STEMI care in Australian hospitals
common_mistakes: Failing to use systematic ECG interpretation approach and missing subtle reciprocal changes
Confusing inferior STEMI with posterior STEMI (which shows tall R waves in V1-V3)
Forgetting to check for contraindications to dual antiplatelet therapy before administration
Delaying STEMI pathway activation while waiting for troponin results - ECG diagnosis is sufficient
equipment_required: Calipers for precise ST segment measurement
ECG reference ranges and normal values chart
